skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The eval and shell-execution alerts are false positives caused by prose, Markdown code fences, and inline code formatting. However, the activation reference promotes coercive prompt injection. The initializer permits path escape, and the packager can include files reached through symlinks.

remediation.issue: The activation guide recommends injecting mandatory and aggressive instructions into every submitted prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Replace forced activation language with transparent, user-controlled matching that cannot override higher-priority instructions.

remediation.issue: The initializer does not validate skill_name before using it as a filesystem path component.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce the documented name pattern and reject absolute paths, separators, dot segments, and resolved paths outside the requested directory.

remediation.issue: The packager follows file symlinks and may add data outside the selected skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks or verify every resolved file remains under the resolved skill directory before adding it.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The guide says “Force Claude to explicitly evaluate each skill” and supplies “MANDATORY” and “CRITICAL” directives. It recommends injecting coercive instructions on every user prompt to manipulate model behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document explicitly recommends forced activation prompts and aggressive wording to make instructions harder for the model to ignore.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Allows Path Escape
semantic_findings.description: The initializer joins an unchecked skill_name to the output path before creating files. Absolute names or dot segments can escape the requested directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CLI value is used directly as a pathlib operand, and no documented name validation is implemented before directory creation.

semantic_findings.title: Archive Packaging Can Follow File Symlinks
semantic_findings.description: The packager accepts any file reported by is_file and writes it to the archive. A symlink can include file contents outside the selected skill directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_file and ZipFile.write follow file symlinks, while the loop performs no resolved-path containment check.

content.value_statement: Designing reliable Agent Skills requires clear triggers, focused instructions, reusable resources, and validation. This skill provides a practical workflow and local scripts for that process.
actual_capabilities: Guides discovery of concrete user requests and trigger conditions.
Explains workflow, task, reference, and capability-based skill structures.
Scaffolds a skill directory with SKILL.md and example resource folders.
Checks frontmatter, skill-name format, activation wording, and validator presence.
Explains progressive disclosure for instructions, references, scripts, and assets.
Provides review, validation-loop, and failure-escalation patterns.
limitations: The packager imports a missing quick_validate module, so packaging may fail in this bundle.
The validator checks only basic frontmatter, naming, trigger wording, and file presence.
The initializer creates placeholder resources that require manual replacement or removal.
The guidance does not test skill activation or output quality automatically.

use_cases.title: Build a First Agent Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a repeated workflow into a structured skill with clear triggers and reusable resources.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skills
use_cases.description: Apply consistent structure, validation, and review patterns across an internal skill library.

use_cases.title: Repair an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Improve activation metadata, reorganize large instructions, and verify required files before release.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Agent Skill named [name] for [workflow]. Ask for missing examples, then scaffold the required files in [directory].
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a first skill from a clear workflow idea

prompt_templates.title: Improve Activation Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [skill path] and improve its name and description. Focus on specific trigger conditions, exclusions, and concise wording.
prompt_templates.scenario: A skill exists but activates inconsistently

prompt_templates.title: Plan Reusable Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these requests: [examples]. Recommend which logic belongs in SKILL.md, scripts, references, or assets, with reasons.
prompt_templates.scenario: Designing a maintainable skill before implementation

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Prepare a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [skill path] for structure, activation, resource design, validation gaps, and security risks. Fix confirmed issues and report remaining limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing an existing skill for controlled release

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing pull requests.
output: Trigger scope: code review requests with a repository or patch
Resources: focused review checklist and optional repository-specific references

output_examples.input: Why does my document skill activate for format conversion?
output_examples.output: The description needs a clear exclusion for conversion tasks and narrower triggers for document creation or tracked-change editing.

output_examples.input: Validate my existing skill before release.
output: Resource layout reviewed for progressive disclosure
Packaging blocked because the bundled validation dependency is missing

best_practices: Start with concrete user requests before choosing structure or bundled resources.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed material into references.
Validate generated files and test the skill on realistic requests before release.
anti_patterns: Do not summarize the entire workflow inside activation metadata.
Do not create scripts, references, or assets without a repeated need.
Do not use coercive prompt language to force skill activation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It can scaffold a skill directory with SKILL.md, scripts, references, assets, and placeholder examples.

faq.question: Can it update an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for trigger metadata, structure, reusable resources, validation, and iteration.

faq.question: Does it validate complete skill behavior?
faq.answer: No. The bundled validator performs basic structural checks and does not measure activation accuracy or output quality.

faq.question: Can it package a skill for distribution?
faq.answer: A packaging script is included, but this bundle lacks its quick_validate dependency and may require repair.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does every skill need scripts, references, and assets?
faq.answer: No. Include only resources that support repeated work, detailed knowledge, or final output files.
